newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks surge to yet another new record.
newsitem.headline: German stocks surge to yet another new record.

text.p: German shares kept up their record-setting pace on Friday, climbing nearly 1.5 percent due to strong overnight Wall Street gains and a German insurance industry merger that fueled fresh demand for domestic shares.
The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 55.14 points, or 1.42 percent, to 3,942.53 points. The DAX had reached a new record high of 3,945.68 points at the outset of floor trade.
In post-bourse electronic trade, the IBIS DAX closed seven points higher at 3,946.73.
The advance was the latest in a string of gains in the DAX index, which ended trade last Friday at 3,795 points.
Although the DAX index is now within sight of a key target at 4,000 points, some traders said the market was likely to take a breather before pushing on to new highs.
Future gains will also depend on the direction of the U.S. share market, which was closed Friday for a national holiday.

Shares in reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG (Munich Re) rose 485 marks in bourse trade to 5,336 marks after announcing it would merge its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit with Victoria Holding AG, creating the second largest primary insurance company in Germany.
The news sparked hopes of further merger activity in the German insurance sector, giving Allianz AG a boost of 27.70 marks to 396.20 marks.

German utility giant RWE AG rose 70 pfennigs to 77.40 marks after announcing 1996/97 group net profit rose seven percent to just under 1.3 billion marks and that sales climbed to 70.8 billion marks from 65.4 billion marks.
Carmakers were generally weaker after recent heady gains. BMW fell 15 marks to 1,460 marks and Volkswagen, Europe's largest carmaker, ended down 11.50 marks to 1,390.50 marks.
